Engine readings run here: understand/quarter_result_q3.json (quarter-review of understand/quarter_case_q3.json) and understand/econ_result_q3.json (econ-review of understand/econ_case_q3.json with econ_options_q3.json). findings.finding: Two engines. (1) An advertising platform: Google advertising 82.0bn of 127.6bn Q3 2026 revenue (64%), Search & other 63.4bn alone 49.7%; Google Services 96.3bn revenue and 39.2bn operating income = 78% of positive segment profit. (2) A capacity-constrained cloud / AI-infrastructure platform: Google Cloud 30.7bn (+103% y/y), segment margin 36.2%, backlog 561bn at 2026-09-30 per the CFO (513.9bn at 2026-06-30 per the 10-Q). The econ review (ads_platform primary, data_platform_software secondary, analyst-selected) cannot close either identity: DAU/ARPU for ads and customer counts / revenue per customer for Cloud are not disclosed; neither model is price-cyclical. Since Q2 2026 Cloud revenue also contains TPU system (hardware) sales recognised on delivery, so Cloud is now part services, part product.

Revenue +25.2bn y/y (+24.7%; +25% in constant currency, so macro/FX is about 0 this quarter, and management expects a slightly larger FX headwind in Q4). Cloud +15.6bn = 62% of the increment; Services +9.3bn (Search & other +6.8bn = +12.0%, subscriptions/platforms/devices +1.4bn = +11.0%, YouTube ads +0.9bn = +9.2%, Network +0.1bn = +1.4%); hedging +0.4bn. Structural: Search (paid demand; query growth claimed by management, paid clicks/CPC for Q3 not yet disclosed), subscriptions (150m+ YouTube Music/Premium subs), Cloud backlog conversion (55% of backlog in 24 months, about 309bn). Mix/reclassification: TPU system product sales inside Cloud (a 'meaningful contributor', amount not disclosed) and Wiz from 2026-03-11; US revenue +39% vs EMEA +9%, APAC +12% is consistent with US-delivered TPU systems. Deceleration in the core: Services growth 16% (Q1) -> 14.5% (Q2) -> 10.6% (Q3), Search 19% -> 16.8% -> 12.0%, YouTube 11% -> 12.9% -> 9.2%; management attributes 'a couple of points' to lapping the late-2025 Search acceleration. Residual: the split of Cloud's +103% into TPU hardware, GCP consumption and Workspace cannot be made from the documents.

Ads: no customer above 10% of revenue (10-K). Cloud: backlog 561bn (+47bn q/q, +3.6x y/y from 155bn), 'the majority related to typical GCP contracts'; just over 55% expected within 24 months (Q2: just over 50%). TPU systems: 'all of the inventory for TPU systems are associated with committed contracts' (inventory 2.4bn -> 13.3bn in nine months); nearly 100 TPU customers; more than 2,600 customers used 100bn+ tokens in 12 months. Firm vs contingent: the backlog is contracted; separately, at 2026-06-30 Alphabet carried contingent exposure to the same AI customer set outside revenue (credit-derivative backstops up to 43.8bn, guarantees 7.6bn, 24.1bn more agreed, a 20.0bn milestone-contingent funding commitment to a private company) and bought 24.2bn of non-marketable securities in 9M 2026 (non-marketable holdings 135.2bn): part of the demand is from companies Alphabet also finances or owns (vendor-financing-like). Backlog concentration by customer and the Q3 update of the contingent items are not disclosed (10-Q pending).

Structural with ad-cycle sensitivity: revenue grew every year FY2020-FY2025 (lowest +8.7% in FY2023); the 2022-23 ad slowdown cut growth and margin (26.5%, 27.4%) but never revenue; the econ review marks neither model price-cyclical; Q3 2026 revenue +25% with Cloud backlog conversion. What is cyclical is the investment cycle: capex 132.0bn in 9M 2026 (FY2026 guide 195-205bn, 2027 to 'increase significantly'), so depreciation (+49% y/y in Q3) and Cloud margins (near-term headwind from third-party capacity) move with the build, not with prices. Carried as a bear mechanism, not as cyclical economics.

Computed mature_growth / stalwart confirmed for the questions (moat, use of excess cash, ROIC on new capital), with a growth/platform overlay: TTM revenue 471.1bn growing about 25% in Q3 with Cloud doubling, i.e. above the stalwart band. The lens stays an FCF DCF with explicit reinvestment, because the business is in a heavy investment phase: TTM capex 159.8bn vs TTM operating cash flow 179.6bn, TTM FCF 19.7bn (company definition), Q3 FCF -9.1bn. The type sets the questions, not a number.

Alphabet gives no revenue, margin, EPS, tax, SBC or share-count guidance; Q4 2026 commentary is qualitative (slightly larger FX headwind; Search lapping 'a couple of points'; TPU system sales scale in Q4 and ramp 'meaningfully' in 2027; Cloud margin headwinds near term; depreciation keeps weighing). The only numeric guide is capex, and its record is: FY2025 initial 75bn -> actual 91.4bn (1.22x the first guide, 0.994x the last mid); Q1 2025 16-18bn -> 17.2bn; FY2026 175-185bn (Feb) -> 180-190bn (Apr) -> 195-205bn (Jul) -> unchanged (Oct), 9M 132.0bn implying Q4 63-73bn. Pattern: first capex guides are raised during the year and the year lands on the last guide; capex guidance is therefore a floor early in a year, not a ceiling. There is no revenue track record to apply.

GAAP EPS 2.12 includes an 8.7bn unrealized loss on equity securities (mainly SpaceX): after tax -6.7bn, -0.55 per share; normalised net income 33.2bn, EPS about 2.67 (quarter-review). Symmetrically, H1 2026 carried +127.5bn YTD equity gains (Q2 +6.26 EPS): TTM EPS 19.16 is 10.95 ex marks. The headline 'operating income +30%' is flattered by lapping the 3.5bn EC fine in Q3 2025 G&A: ex that fine, Alphabet operating income grew about 17% (34.7bn -> 40.6bn) and the Services margin fell from about 42.5% to 40.7% (Services operating income +5.8% ex fine); current-year legal charges partly offset (amount not given). Operating margin 31.8% vs 34.0% in Q2; operating income -0.5% q/q on revenue +6.5% q/q (depreciation +49% y/y, Other Bets loss 2.05bn, Alphabet-level costs 7.66bn +71%). SBC 8.63bn = 6.8% of revenue (+36% y/y) is a real cost. Cash: Q3 FCF -9.1bn, FCF / normalised net income -0.27; OCF also carried a 5.2bn EC fine cash payment (accrued earlier, cash not P&L). Against attributed consensus (AV, n=44, basis not named) EPS 2.12 sat below the lowest estimate 2.25; ex the mark 2.67 is still about 11% under the 3.00 mean, while revenue 127.6bn was in line with 127.8bn: the miss is in costs and depreciation, not demand.

findings.topic: forensic screens, ROIC and incremental ROIC
findings.finding: Piotroski 7 of 8 (strong; the failed signal is leverage), Altman Z'' 6.8 (safe), Beneish unavailable (inputs missing), Rule of 40 not applicable. ROIC (prefetch definition: NOPAT / equity + debt - cash) 28.9% in FY2025, average 29.3%, incremental FY2023-25 21.8%. The 2026 build lowers the incremental return for now: from 2025-12-31 to 2026-09-30 PP&E rose 126.2bn (246.6 -> 372.8bn), goodwill + intangibles 32.3bn (Wiz), while TTM operating income rose 28.0bn (129.0 -> 157.0bn), about 23bn after tax: roughly 15% on the new operating capital, before most of it produces revenue (a lag-affected reading, not a run rate). Equity-based ROIC is distorted by the unrealized marks in equity (non-marketable 135.2bn, SpaceX stock). Management expects ROIC 'meaningfully above our cost of capital' (statement, not evidence).

Search: worldwide referral search share about 90% vs Bing 5.3% (StatCounter, attributed; does not count AI assistants); Google Search & other +12% vs Microsoft search and news advertising ex-TAC +12% in the same quarter. Advertising budgets: Google advertising +10.6% vs Meta advertising +25.9% (Q3 2026), so Google is losing relative share in the Google+Meta pool (59.7% -> 56.5%): the ads moat holds on level and margin (Services 40.7%), not on share gains. Cloud/AI compute: Google Cloud +103% (incl. TPU hardware) vs Azure +48% and Oracle OCI +121%, segment margin 36.2% vs 23.7% a year ago; the evidenced moat source is owned silicon (TPU, sold as systems since Q2 2026) plus contracted backlog, against AWS Trainium and Microsoft/Oracle GPU capacity. AWS Q3 is not yet reported. Returns fading toward the cost of capital is the default unless the TPU cost advantage shows up in Cloud margin after depreciation.

Capital return has stopped and outside capital funds the build: buybacks 0 in 9M 2026 (39.8bn in 9M 2025); Q3 ATM sales 12m Class A + 24m Class C shares for 12.4bn net (27.6bn of the 40bn programme left); senior notes 28.7bn net in Q3; long-term debt 46.5bn (2025-12-31) -> 125.1bn; 6.25% mandatory convertible preferred (19m x 1,000) adds 298m of preferred dividends a quarter and converts about 2029; June 2026 equity raise 49.6bn net. Shares outstanding 12,088m -> 12,294m (+1.7% in nine months), diluted weighted shares +1.4% y/y; buybacks minus SBC -8.6bn in Q3. Quarterly interest expense 967m vs interest income 1.77bn. Acquisitions 34.1bn in 9M 2026 (Wiz). Promise vs delivery: in July management said it was not planning to return to equity markets beyond the ATM; in Q3 it used the ATM for 12.4bn (consistent).

Cash, equivalents and marketable securities 265.1bn at 2026-09-30 (cash 56.3bn), but marketable securities include SpaceX stock under sale restrictions (80.0bn short-term and 14.1bn to Q3 2027 at 2026-06-30, before the Q3 -8.7bn mark; Q3 split is a 10-Q gap); non-marketable securities 135.2bn. Spendable liquidity is roughly 170bn against long-term debt 125.1bn. Fixed commitments grew: purchase commitments 924bn at quarter end per the CFO (811bn at 2026-06-30, 707bn of it fixed, mostly through 2030), plus data-center leases not yet commenced; these costs stay if demand slips. Legal: US Search remedies (cross-appeals) touch Search & other (49.7% of revenue), ad tech remedies touch Network (5.8%); EC Android fine 5.2bn paid in cash in Q3.

economics.reason: Revenue grew every year FY2020-FY2025 (lowest +8.7% in FY2023); the 2022-23 ad slowdown hit growth and margin but not revenue; Q3 2026 revenue +25% (+25% constant currency) with Cloud backlog of 561bn (just over 55% in 24 months) and TPU inventory tied to committed contracts; neither econ model is price-cyclical. The AI capacity-investment cycle (capex, depreciation, commitments) is a bear mechanism, not cyclical economics.
